title: 9 source lines exceed 100 columns and werkzeug exceptions are imported inside function bodies

title: Unhandled server errors escape the JSON error contract; /health cannot report unhealthy
evidence: app.py:49 registers the JSON error handler for HTTPException only, so a sqlite3.OperationalError raised by app.py:88 `get_db().execute("SELECT 1")` in health() propagates as a plain 500 HTML page rather than {"error": ...}; health() has no try/except and no degraded-status branch
suggestion: Add a second `@app.errorhandler(Exception)` returning JSON 500, and have health() catch sqlite3.Error to return 503 {"status": "unhealthy"} instead of raising.

title: No busy_timeout set on per-request SQLite connections
evidence: app.py:28 `g.db = sqlite3.connect(database, uri=use_uri)` takes the driver default (0s busy timeout); the dev server at app.py:134 is threaded by default, so concurrent writers can surface `database is locked` immediately
suggestion: Pass `timeout=5.0` to sqlite3.connect (or `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`) so concurrent writes retry rather than failing.

title: ?author= filter is exact and case-sensitive by design
